Trying before choosing.
When our school opened a hobby afternoon, I wanted to join every group. There were painting tables, board games, model making and a quiz. My friend Jo suggested that we try just two activities before choosing a club. I agreed, although I thought a real hobby should be something I was already good at. First, we tried painting. I enjoy drawing, but using many colors together was new to me. My first picture looked strange. The club leader did not tell me to start again. She asked what I wanted to show and helped me choose fewer colors. I finished painting a small garden. Next, we joined the board game table. I wanted to learn chess, but the rules seemed difficult. A member showed me one move at a time. Jo learned faster than me, yet nobody made it a race. By the end, I could play a short practice game. I chose the painting club because I liked creating something of my own. Jo chose chess. We planned to show each other what we learned each week. I discovered that enjoying a hobby did not mean being the best immediately. It meant wanting to keep trying and noticing small improvements.
